title: Coefficient maps between computing cup resolutions
statement: For a scheme X and module morphisms phi:F→F1 and psi:G→G1, there exist computing pairings D for F,G and E for F1,G1 [def-sc-module-cup-resolution-data] and cochain maps l:D.left.K→E.left.K, r:D.right.K→E.right.K and t:D.target.K→E.target.K. In every degree these maps on global cocycles induce respectively H(phi), H(psi), and H(phi tensor psi) under the computing class maps [def-sc-ringed-space-module-cohomology]. For every open V and bidegree p,q, t(p+q)(D.pair(p,q,V)(a,b))=E.pair(p,q,V)(l(p)(a),r(q)(b)). This is simultaneous functorial resolution data, with no specified bilinear map on cohomology and no quasi-coherence or flatness hypothesis.

source.place: Section 20.31, naive cup product and Lemma 20.31.3; functorial Godement construction in Section 20.30 (0FKR)

lean.statement:
theorem moduleCup_coefficient_resolution_maps (X : Scheme.{v})
    (F G F₁ G₁ : X.Modules) (φ : F ⟶ F₁) (ψ : G ⟶ G₁) :
    ∃ (D : CupResolutionPairing F G) (E : CupResolutionPairing F₁ G₁)
      (l : D.left.K ⟶ E.left.K) (r : D.right.K ⟶ E.right.K)
      (t : D.target.K ⟶ E.target.K),
      (∀ (n : ℕ)
        (a : ((((RingedSpace.globalSectionsFunctor X.toRingedSpace).mapHomologicalComplex
          (ComplexShape.up ℕ)).obj D.left.K).sc n).moduleCatLeftHomologyData.K)
        (a' : ((((RingedSpace.globalSectionsFunctor X.toRingedSpace).mapHomologicalComplex
          (ComplexShape.up ℕ)).obj E.left.K).sc n).moduleCatLeftHomologyData.K),
        a'.val = (l.f n).val.app (op ⊤) a.val →
          E.left.class n a' =
            (RingedSpace.moduleCohomology X.toRingedSpace n).map φ (D.left.class n a)) ∧
      (∀ (n : ℕ)
        (b : ((((RingedSpace.globalSectionsFunctor X.toRingedSpace).mapHomologicalComplex
          (ComplexShape.up ℕ)).obj D.right.K).sc n).moduleCatLeftHomologyData.K)
        (b' : ((((RingedSpace.globalSectionsFunctor X.toRingedSpace).mapHomologicalComplex
          (ComplexShape.up ℕ)).obj E.right.K).sc n).moduleCatLeftHomologyData.K),
        b'.val = (r.f n).val.app (op ⊤) b.val →
          E.right.class n b' =
            (RingedSpace.moduleCohomology X.toRingedSpace n).map ψ (D.right.class n b)) ∧
      (∀ (n : ℕ)
        (c : ((((RingedSpace.globalSectionsFunctor X.toRingedSpace).mapHomologicalComplex
          (ComplexShape.up ℕ)).obj D.target.K).sc n).moduleCatLeftHomologyData.K)
        (c' : ((((RingedSpace.globalSectionsFunctor X.toRingedSpace).mapHomologicalComplex
          (ComplexShape.up ℕ)).obj E.target.K).sc n).moduleCatLeftHomologyData.K),
        c'.val = (t.f n).val.app (op ⊤) c.val →
          E.target.class n c' =
            (RingedSpace.moduleCohomology X.toRingedSpace n).map
              (@id (F ⊗ G ⟶ F₁ ⊗ G₁) (φ ⊗ₘ ψ)) (D.target.class n c)) ∧
      (∀ (p q : ℕ) (V : X.Opens)
        (a : Γ(D.left.K.X p, V)) (b : Γ(D.right.K.X q, V)),
        (t.f (p + q)).val.app (op V) (D.pair p q V a b) =
          E.pair p q V ((l.f p).val.app (op V) a) ((r.f q).val.app (op V) b))

proof.text: Obtain simultaneous augmented flasque integer tensor complexes and coefficient maps from moduleCup_godement_coefficient_complexes. Restrict the six complexes and maps to natural degrees. Identify the restricted single complex with single0 and prove augmentation naturality on degree-zero components. Curry tensor sections followed by the tensor summand inclusion and raw pairing. Prove restriction compatibility using sheaf morphism naturality and signed Leibniz using the total tensor differential. The raw zero-degree formula supplies augmentation_pair.

Construct each injective comparison explicitly by InjectiveResolution.descOfQuasiIso of the identity. Flasque source terms and injective target terms are right-acyclic, and the acyclic-resolution comparison criterion gives isomorphisms on global homology. Package these comparisons and section pairings into D and E.

Construct a comparison homotopy for a quasi-isomorphic nonnegative augmented source and injective target. Degree-zero and positive-degree exact sequences of the source allow extension through each differential to build a nullhomotopy for a map vanishing on the augmentation. Apply this to the difference of the coefficient map followed by the target comparison and the source comparison followed by an injective lift. Global sections preserves the homotopy, so homology maps agree. ModuleCat cycles isomorphisms and naturality of the homology projection identify the mapped concrete cycle. InjectiveResolution.isoRightDerivedObj_inv_naturality gives the class equation for any map over a coefficient morphism. Apply it to the three restricted coefficient maps.

Evaluate the raw tensor-chain square on a tensor summand in bidegree (p,q). The tensorHom component sends tensor sections to the tensor of mapped sections. Restriction to natural degrees yields the section pairing equation. Assemble the five existential witnesses and four conjunctions.

proof_origin.place: Explicit flasque comparison packaging, comparison homotopy and class naturality proved in Lean; raw functorial tensor construction isolated separately
